findings: Own normal hand play has an unconditional normal-return call sequence PlayCardFromHand -> ExecuteAutoPlayCards -> CreateAction_PlayCardFromHand_End in BP_PlayerMoves.

Each verified own action End wrapper calls send, then its local ReceiveAction with receiveFromLocal=true, then OnXActionFinished. No wait for an HTTP completion is present in these caller exec chains.
CreateAction_SendActionWithSub converges on StopActionProcess before any syntactically reachable normal return; matching non-tutorial includeMatchState=false passes AddActionWithSub first.

Both hand-target and draw-selection replies run optional AfterWait before autoplay. Draw-selection then runs HandleExtraPlayTriggersAfterSelectHandCard; its End wrapper also resolves the pending draw queue before send.

PlayerMoves.DoNextInQueue is a distinct autoplay caller: each loop iteration calls CreateAction_PlayCardFromHand_Start -> PlayCardFromHand -> End before advancing. Do not conflate this with OnlineMatch.ExecuteAutoPlayCards inside the requesting action.
All three receive functions call DoSubActions with the forwarded receiveFromLocal flag; RULE189 establishes the shared limiter application loop.

Existing engine ApplyPendingGotchaPlayReceipts sites approximate these local receipt boundaries, but are not a general ordered subaction consumer. Deferred selections and nested effects use a different shared depth mechanism.
limits: Parsed-pak static control flow only, assuming valid context and normal returns. Calls are not inlined; branch conditions abstracted except the three explicitly recorded normal-send assumptions.
No assertion that every live action routes here, or that errors, native calls, asynchronous/latent behavior, reentry or disconnected paths are semantically modeled.
Full pending-draw queue implementation, action marker insertion, nested receive reentry, ActionProcess flag changes from callbacks and all other subaction consumers remain unverified.

Do not simply flush limiter updates on outer EndEffectResolution: it drains selection replies, while native first-action receipt precedes those replies. Need an ordered action consumer that preserves the separate reply boundaries.
